newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai halts two A share firms on abnormal price.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai halts two A share firms on abnormal price.

text.p: The Shanghai stock exchange on Thursday suspended trading in the shares of two domestic A share firms for one day because of abnormal price movements in the past few days, an exchange statement said.
The exchange will investigate the price movements of Petroleum Long Champ (Group) Co and Shao Xing Department Store Co, the statement said.
It was the second time the exchange has suspended trading in selected stocks in the past week.

Last Friday, the exchange halted trading in shares of Shenyang Neu-Alpine Software Co and Hebei Weiyuan Industry Co for half a day, the first time in its history that the bourse had suspended stocks for "abnormal price movements".

China's securities authorities are introducing measures to cool stock trading after rises of more than 50 percent in the share indices on the Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges in the first four months of this year despite repeated official warnings.
On Wednesday, Beijing announced a ban on state enterprises and listed firms trading on the stock markets.
